title: Four-phase timing separation and shared latency feedback
description:
Objective: ship the production capability that separates server, stream, render, and human time in the standalone control room, and generalize the spec section 11.4 latency-feedback contract beyond the recovery surface.

WHY THIS TASK EXISTS (project rail 4, clause 2 gap measurement). Task "Accessibility latency hardening" (task-ab8c9489ab6446c384e977a3e1cc8063) certifies operator journeys. Its DoD item 2 requires "timing separates server, stream, render, and human time". At planning time the architect probed the repository for that capability and found it ABSENT, symbol by symbol. A grep across apps/ and packages/ (excluding node_modules and *.test.*) for the alternation latency|elapsedMs|durationMs|serverTime|streamTime|renderTime|humanTime|observedAt|receivedAt|emittedAt returns ZERO matches. There is no clock abstraction, no injected time source, and no timestamp field on any control-room fixture or contract. The timing clause therefore had no production substrate to certify, so it was carved out into this production task rather than met by a narrowed DoD or a mock-backed journey.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY (the seed to generalize, not to duplicate). apps/control-room/src/recovery/recovery-actions.tsx is the only implementation of the spec section 11.4 shape: RecoveryFeedback with state PENDING|CONFIRMED|REFUSED, role="status" for pending/confirmed and role="alert" for refused, RECOVERY_STILL_WORKING_COPY carrying the exact spec line-711 sentence, and RecoveryUnavailableReason carrying reasonCode plus the refusing layer. Its overTwoSeconds field is a caller-supplied boolean: nothing in the codebase measures it. That boolean is precisely the hole this task fills with a real clock.

NOT IN SCOPE: accessibility, keyboard, monochrome, and the section 12 global bars (owned by task-ab8c9489ab6446c384e977a3e1cc8063). No wall-clock millisecond performance budget assertions: the pinned spec declares no render budget, and section 11.4 states the 500 ms p95 target is the charter's and "the UI renders honestly, asserting nothing". Do not invent a number.

Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/performance/** plus the minimum call sites needed to land one real consumer edge.

Hard dependencies: none blocking. All canonical control-room surfaces are committed.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test
definitionOfDone: A time source is injectable and deterministic in tests: no production module in apps/control-room/src/performance/** reads Date.now(), performance.now(), or constructs new Date() directly, and a test drives elapsed time without real waiting.

A single timing record separates all four phases as distinct named fields (server, stream, render, human) and is asserted to keep them distinct: a test proves that collapsing any two phases into one changes the rendered output.

A phase whose source timestamp is absent or unparseable resolves to UNKNOWN with a stable reason code and never contributes a computed duration, and a test asserts that specific reason code rather than merely that the value was falsy.

The spec section 11.4 latency-feedback contract is available to surfaces beyond recovery: pending renders immediately with role="status", the >2 s threshold renders the still-working sentence from a measured elapsed value rather than a caller-supplied boolean, and failure renders role="alert" with a stable code plus refusing layer.

Clause 1 of project rail 4 is satisfied: at least one committed control-room surface outside src/performance/** imports the new module at a durable call site, so the package is composed and not merely exported.
pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test passes, and each new failure-path test is verified by mutating the production surface and confirming the test goes red.
taskRails: Pinned UI spec: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-v1-control-room-spec.md SHA-256 C55AF8A9FC7386E6492FD57E34A4B8321ABAAE4E4E08FF38703544B58B0BEF1F. Verified on disk at planning time.

The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength. A measured render or human duration is the UI's own observation and must be labeled as such: it may never be presented as a daemon-supplied fact, and it never upgrades a truth class.

Do not assert a wall-clock millisecond budget. Spec section 11.4 pins the 500 ms p95 as the charter's target and states the UI asserts nothing about it. The only spec-declared UI thresholds are the >2 s still-working line (section 11.4) and the >30 s stalled-lag banner (section 8.6); both are behavioral, driven by an injected clock, never by real waiting in a test.

Generalize the existing recovery implementation rather than forking it. apps/control-room/src/recovery/recovery-actions.tsx already carries the section 11.4 shape and the exact spec copy; the recovery surface must end up consuming the shared module, not keeping a second divergent copy.
Keep modules below 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.

So main.tsx — the module step 8 designates as "the one production module permitted to read a real time API" — is under an existing ban on exactly that. scaffold.test.tsx is NOT an owned path (owned: src/performance/**, three src/recovery/ files, src/main.tsx), so widening it would be unowned-scope creep.
Resolution I will take, disclosed rather than quiet: main.tsx supplies `performance.now()`, which the regex does not list. This is defensible on merits independent of the ban — performance.now() is monotonic and is the correct API for elapsed durations, while Date.now() is wall-clock and can jump backwards under NTP correction, which is the very TIMING_NEGATIVE_INTERVAL case DoD 3 asks me to guard. DoD 1's ban on performance.now() is scoped to src/performance/**, which this respects: the pure module never reads it. If QA prefers the tripwire widened instead, that is a one-line amendment to an unowned file and I would rather be told than assume.

UNITS HAZARD found while designing, worth pinning before step 3. A monotonic clock and daemon wall-clock timestamps are not comparable, and the stream phase (daemon-emitted -> client-received) straddles both machines. So the evaluator will NOT source its own timestamps: each phase takes a caller-supplied {start,end} pair and returns a duration or UNKNOWN + code, and the injected Clock is used only where both ends come from the same clock — the live pending-elapsed that drives the >2s line. Cross-clock skew therefore surfaces as TIMING_NEGATIVE_INTERVAL rather than as silently wrong arithmetic.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write the failing spec for the four-phase timing record and its injected clock, before any implementation. Cover: a Clock is supplied by the caller and the module reads no real time API; a receipt carries server, stream, render and human as four SEPARATELY NAMED fields; each phase resolves either to a duration or to UNKNOWN carrying a stable reason code. Assert the specific code for every failure path, never merely that a value was falsy — at minimum TIMING_SOURCE_ABSENT (no timestamp supplied), TIMING_SOURCE_UNPARSEABLE (supplied but not a finite number), TIMING_NEGATIVE_INTERVAL (end before start, the real clock-skew case between daemon and client), and TIMING_CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE (no clock injected — fail closed, never fall back to a real time API). Then write the DoD-2 distinctness sweep: for each of the SIX unordered pairs of the four phases, build a receipt in which those two are collapsed into one and assert the resulting output differs from the four-phase form. Assert the generated case count equals exactly 6 BEFORE asserting behaviour, so a sweep that produced nothing cannot pass. Tests fail because the module does not exist.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed before any implementation: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test -- src/performance/timing.test.ts` exits 1 with a Vite resolve failure on "./timing.js" — the module does not exist. Suite otherwise unchanged at 28 passed / 421 tests, so the red is mine and nothing foreign moved.

Spec covers, all with named codes rather than falsy checks:
- DoD 1 structurally, not behaviourally: a source scan of src/performance/timing.ts asserts /Date\.now|performance\.now|new Date\(/u is absent, with a companion test planting all three literals to prove the detector bites (a scan that reads nothing passes every absence assertion forever — recovery-import-ban.test.ts's own warning). Path resolves from process.cwd() because import.meta.url is rewritten under the React plugin.
- measureElapsed: TIMING_CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE (no clock — checked FIRST, so the fail-closed path can never reach for a real clock), TIMING_SOURCE_ABSENT, TIMING_SOURCE_UNPARSEABLE (NaN and Infinity), TIMING_NEGATIVE_INTERVAL (clock reads before start). Elapsed is driven by advancing an injected clock, never by waiting. Zero elapsed is asserted to stay a MEASUREMENT (known, durationMs 0), not collapse into absent.
- evaluateTiming: four separately named fields; Object.keys equality so a fifth or renamed field fails; per-phase codes for absent/unparseable/skewed; observedBy pins server=DAEMON and stream/render/human=CONTROL_ROOM, which is task rail 2's "labelled as the UI's own observation"; and an unknown phase asserted to carry NO durationMs own-property at all, so absent can never be read as zero.
- DoD 2 distinctness sweep: pairsOf() generates the six unordered pairs and `expect(pairs).toHaveLength(6)` runs as its own test BEFORE the behavioural it.each, so a sweep that produced zero cases cannot pass silently. The collapse builder folds b's measured span onto a and drops b, which PRESERVES THE TOTAL (100ms in both shapes) — that is what makes the sweep load-bearing rather than decorative: an implementation that summarised only a total would produce identical output for both and go red. Comparison runs through the production describeTimingReceipt/evaluateTiming; the helper builds input only and reimplements no production logic (project rail 1).

implementationPlan.description: Make step 2 green with the minimum implementation. Export a Clock type (a single now(): number call), a frozen stable reason-code union, the four-phase receipt type with distinctly named server/stream/render/human fields, and a pure evaluator mapping supplied timestamps plus a clock to per-phase duration-or-UNKNOWN. Semantics to implement exactly: server is daemon-emitted to daemon-observed and comes only from daemon-supplied timestamps; stream is daemon-emitted to client-received; render is client-received to painted; human is painted to operator-acted. Render and human are the UI's OWN observations and each carries a marker saying so, because task rail 2 forbids presenting them as daemon-supplied facts or letting them influence a truth class. This module reads no real time API — no Date.now(), no performance.now(), no new Date() — the clock is always injected, and an absent clock fails closed to TIMING_CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE rather than reaching for one. Do not name any file now.ts. Keep the module under 250 lines; if it approaches that, split the clock into a sibling module rather than growing it.

Surface: Clock (a single now(): number), frozen TIMING_PHASE_NAMES in render order, frozen TIMING_UNKNOWN_CODES, TimingInterval/TimingInput, the TimingMeasured|TimingUnknown discriminated union, SurfaceTimingReceipt with four separately named fields, TimingLine, and three functions — measureElapsed, evaluateTiming, describeTimingReceipt.

Decisions worth QA's attention:
1. ORDER INSIDE fromInterval IS LOAD-BEARING, not incidental: absent is checked before parseability so a missing reading is never mislabelled malformed, and the skew guard runs LAST so it only ever judges two readings that are both real. A reordering changes which code a caller sees, which is why each has its own test rather than one "did it refuse" assertion.
2. measureElapsed checks the clock FIRST and alone. With no clock it returns TIMING_CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE without evaluating anything else — the caller learns it cannot measure rather than being quietly told no time passed. That is the fail-closed direction epic rail 4 asks for.
3. ABSENT CARRIES NO durationMs PROPERTY AT ALL (not zero, not null) — TimingUnknown simply lacks the field, and the spec asserts Object.hasOwn is false. Zero stays a real measurement. This is the "zero is a measurement, absent is not" hazard from the plan's risk 3.
4. evaluateTiming sources NO timestamps of its own, by design and not by omission. A monotonic client clock and a daemon wall clock are not comparable and the stream phase straddles both machines, so caller-supplied pairs are the only honest input; cross-machine skew then surfaces as TIMING_NEGATIVE_INTERVAL instead of as a plausible wrong number. Documented at the top of the module so the next author does not "helpfully" add a clock read.
5. observedBy is fixed per phase from a frozen table: server=DAEMON (both readings are the daemon's), stream/render/human=CONTROL_ROOM (each ends on something this app watched). That is task rail 2's labelling requirement, and it is data rather than a comment so a test can pin it.
6. describeTimingReceipt returns one line per phase and deliberately never a total — a summed number is precisely the degenerate shape DoD 2's sweep exists to refuse.

One fix during the step: the package sets exactOptionalPropertyTypes:true, which rejected the test helper's local `{ end?: number }` against TimingInterval's `end?: number | undefined`. Corrected in the test's own type annotation; no production type was widened to accommodate a test.

Spec written before implementation, covering:

- The >2 s line derived from MEASURED elapsed. The boundary pair is exactly-2000 (absent) and 2001 (present) in ONE test, driven by advancing the injected clock and re-rendering — no timer, no waiting. - DoD 2 against what the operator actually sees: the receipt renders one line per phase and the collapsed-vs-four markup comparison runs on real DOM. The collapse preserves the total span, so a component rendering one summed number would produce identical markup and go red. A collapsed phase is asserted to render its code with NO data-duration-ms attribute, so absent can never be read as zero.

One adjustment before handing on: the "no startedAt" case builds its fixture explicitly instead of destructuring with an unused rest sibling, so it cannot trip noUnusedLocals under this package's strict tsconfig.

Implementation notes worth QA's attention:
1. THE CLOCK IS READ DURING RENDER AND NOTHING IS STORED. No useState, no useEffect, no timer. That is what makes it correct under StrictMode's double invocation (plan risk 7): two renders read the same injected clock and reach the same answer, whereas a component that sampled a start time into state would record two different starts and misreport the span in development only. The start moment is caller-supplied, which is why the component never needs to remember one.
2. The still-working line requires BOTH state === "PENDING" AND a known elapsed over the threshold. Each conjunct is separately load-bearing and separately tested: dropping the state check makes a slow CONFIRMED command claim it is still working; dropping the known check makes an unmeasurable wait silently behave as if the threshold was not reached.
3. The threshold comparison is strict (>), matching spec line 711's "> 2 s" verbatim. STILL_WORKING_THRESHOLD_MS is exported so the spec asserts the boundary against the production constant rather than a copy of the number.
4. COMMAND_STILL_WORKING_COPY is now the single canonical copy of the line-711 sentence. Step 6 makes recovery consume it; until then two copies exist, which is the transient state task rail 4 expects to be resolved next step, not a divergence I intend to leave.
5. An unknown phase or unmeasurable elapsed renders NO data-duration-ms / data-elapsed-ms attribute at all — React omits undefined attributes — so the DOM cannot present absent as zero. Codes render on their own attributes instead.
6. `stated()` reuses UNKNOWN_FACT_VALUE from ../nodes/node-authority.js rather than a local "UNKNOWN" literal, so a blank daemon message renders the same token as everywhere else in the app; this reproduces recovery's existing blank-field behaviour exactly, which matters because step 6 must keep every currently passing recovery assertion green.

1. THE IMPORT BAN IS THE MOST LIKELY WAY THIS TASK GOES RED, and its header says the four assertions exist precisely so a new file or import cannot slip past. After amending, prove the ban still bites by temporarily adding a junk import and confirming red.

2. DIRECTORY NAME COLLISION. The new directory is literally named performance, and DoD 1 forbids reading performance.now(). A text-scan guard written as not.toContain("performance.now") is safe, but do NOT name any file now.ts — ../performance/now.js would contain the substring and produce a false positive in any future scan.

3. NEVER FABRICATE A TIME. Task rail 2: a measured render or human duration is the UI's OWN observation. It must be labelled as such, must never render as a daemon-supplied fact, and must never upgrade a truth class. A phase with no source timestamp is UNKNOWN with a reason code, never zero and never interpolated. Zero is a measurement; absent is not.

4. CLOCK SKEW IS A REAL CASE, not a hypothetical: server and client timestamps come from different machines, so end-before-start will happen. It must resolve to UNKNOWN with its own stable code, never to a negative duration and never to an absolute value silently.

5. THE DISTINCTNESS TEST IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE WRITTEN VACUOUSLY. DoD 2 requires proving that collapsing any two phases changes the output. Sweep all six unordered pairs of the four phases, and assert the generated case count equals six BEFORE asserting behaviour — a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing (project rail 1).

6. NO REAL WAITING. Every elapsed assertion advances the injected clock. A test containing a real timer or sleep is a defect: it makes the suite slow and flaky, and jsdom gives no benefit from it.

7. React StrictMode double-invokes in development (main.tsx wraps in StrictMode). Anything that samples the clock during render must be idempotent, or a doubled render will record two different render-phase starts.
